# P05 — Colonial administration, princely institutions and public life

**Window:** 1792–1946 CE; editorial window needing local refinements.

**Question:** Which administrations and communities generated records for different parts of the modern territory?

## Evidence presently available in this seed

Archive portals, manuals and later archaeological histories provide source routes. No claim is made that this starter has audited a complete colonial series.

Source routes: [S013](../sources/S013.md), [S028](../sources/S028.md), [S029](../sources/S029.md), [S030](../sources/S030.md), [S031](../sources/S031.md), [S033](../sources/S033.md).

## What this does not establish

The chosen window is an organizational convention, not a uniformly verified regime boundary. Gazetteer descriptions and censuses reflect administrative categories and do not speak for every community.

## Research tasks

- [ ] Inventory district manuals, revenue proceedings, censuses, gazettes, court records and newspapers by volume and year.
- [ ] Separate British-administered Malabar from Travancore and Cochin institutions.
- [ ] Study reform, labour, slavery, caste, gender and resistance with multiple independent source traditions.
- [ ] Do not restrict inclusion to people described as Malayali or records written in Malayalam.
